closed_blockers.blocker: WeasyPrint was believed unable to run on this machine, because importing it fails with 'cannot load library libgobject-2.0-0', no GTK runtime is installed, and WSL2 is disabled at the BIOS level.
closed_blockers.resolution: The premise was wrong. Since Python 3.8, Windows DLL resolution for ctypes and cffi ignores PATH, so putting a GLib and Pango directory on PATH looks correct and does nothing. os.add_dll_directory() works. Tesseract-OCR bundles the complete stack WeasyPrint needs, so pointing add_dll_directory at 'C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR' before importing weasyprint is sufficient. Implemented in docs/Defense/REV22/render.py.
closed_blockers.proof_that_it_is_faithful: A byte-identical copy of the REV21 source HTML was rendered here and compared against the locked REV21 PDF across all 13 slides and 538 text spans. Maximum positional drift 0.0000 pt, zero text mismatches.
closed_blockers.note: WeasyPrint output is not bit-reproducible, so two renders of the same input differ in bytes. Hash equality is the wrong test; span geometry is the right one.

audit_result_in_one_paragraph: No blocker and no major defect. Every number on the deck was verified twice, once mechanically by the operator against the byte-exact thesis tables and once independently by a web call, with zero exceptions across 136 items on slides 6 to 13. Chart geometry was measured directly from the PDF drawing objects and every plotted point lands within a hundredth of a point. All twelve citations exist with the correct year and support the proposition they are attached to. No slide asserts causation, claims an established mechanism, or reads the payment-method result as strict cash specificity. What remained was four cosmetic wording items, now fixed in REV22, and one substantial exposure in the question period that is not a deck problem.

single_most_important_finding.what: An examiner can ask what evidence there is that the CEO knew about the acquisition at the pre-announcement call.
single_most_important_finding.why_it_bites: The event clock is anchored on the announcement date. The thesis observes neither when negotiations began nor when the chief executive learned of the deal.
single_most_important_finding.route: Slide 12 box 3 states the boundary in one line: the data mark the announcement date, not when negotiations began. Both rebuttals go in the speaker notes. Rebuttal 1, the only one that answers the real direction of the attack: misflagged calls dilute a binary treatment indicator and drag the estimate toward zero, so the effect was found despite the flaw. Rebuttal 2, narrower than it looks: the flat PRE2 against the significant PRE1 shows the signal is tightly timed with no pre-trend.
single_most_important_finding.found_by: The examiner pass, run blind. The operator had not anticipated it.
single_most_important_finding.recorded_on_the_deck: REV22 slide 12, box 3, The anticipatory window
single_most_important_finding.trap_do_not_repeat: A flat PRE2 catches negotiations that began EARLIER than the window. It says nothing about negotiations that began AFTER the flagged call, which is the direction the limitation states, because such a firm contributes nothing to PRE1 and nothing to PRE2 alike. A significant PRE1 does not rule it out either, since PRE1 is an average and contamination attenuates rather than flattens it. A guard clause making this mistake was shipped on slide 12 and removed as R22-10. Do not reintroduce it.

speaker_notes_brief_when_that_work_start.time_budget: 18 minutes with a 2 minute buffer inside a hard 20 minute limit. Sections are 5 minutes for slides 1 to 5, 10 minutes for slides 6 to 10, and 3 minutes for slides 11 to 13.
speaker_notes_brief_when_that_work_start.word_budget_method: Do not invent a per-slide time. Measure the presenter's own speaking rate on two timed passages, take the lower clean rate, and multiply by 17 minutes to leave a minute for pauses and navigation. Allocate by the 5:10:3 section ratio. The measurement is an input only the presenter can supply; do not fake it from an assumed rate.
speaker_notes_brief_when_that_work_start.grounding_rule: Every academic sentence and every number in the notes must trace to an exact thesis file and location. Where the thesis is silent, the notes must say so rather than fill the gap.
speaker_notes_brief_when_that_work_start.hard_constraint: The notes may explain the visible slide. They may not add a result, a mechanism, a causal claim, or an appendix-only analysis to the main talk.
speaker_notes_brief_when_that_work_start.committee_context: One examiner prefers defenses that finish promptly, so a tight findings-forward delivery matters more than completeness.
speaker_notes_brief_when_that_work_start.step_one_before_anything_else: docs/Defense/SPEAKING_RATE_TEST.md. Two timed passages, one prose and one number-heavy, read aloud by Sina. Nothing else about the notes can be correct until this is done.
speaker_notes_brief_when_that_work_start.what_null_means: The measurement has not happened. Do not draft notes. Do not assume a rate. Ask Sina to run SPEAKING_RATE_TEST.md and record both times and both rates here first.

built_after_the_audit: Every exchange is now two files each way: PROMPT_<time>.md plus one inputs archive up, main JSON plus one outputs archive down. expected_artifacts must be empty or a single .zip and prepare refuses anything else.

The side panel shows each running call as a checklist of expected files, ticked with a size as they land, and holds Done disabled until they have all arrived. Done stopping monitoring was the failure that cost a call; it is now visible instead of invisible.

web_call_infrastructure.lesson_for_any_future_call: Because inputs travel as an archive now, always require an inventory of extracted filenames with byte sizes before any answer. An archive gets extracted, glanced at, and answered from unless something makes a shallow read visible.

three_attenuation_arguments_it_records: Q2 generated regressand: the residual is the dependent variable, so there is no coefficient bias, but first-stage noise inflates outcome noise and biases against finding the run-up.
Q13 speaker misattribution: adds noise to the outcome, attenuating toward zero.
Section 2.3 conservative floor: if anticipation leaks into the vetted script, the residual understates the signal, so the measure is a floor and not a ceiling.
A fourth, inverted, at Q12: if media rumor had made deals effectively public, the PRE1 to GAP contrast would be blunted rather than sharp. Here it is the absence of attenuation that helps.
defense_ledger.condition_on_all_of_them: They hold only while the noise is unrelated to deal timing. Noise that systematically tracks the pre-announcement window is a confound, not noise, and it runs the other way. The thesis claims no mechanism, which is what limits the damage.

findings_that_change_what_to_say_not_wha.F01: The attenuation rebuttal was stated flatly. Misclassification attenuates only when it is nondifferential, and negotiation onset is unobserved, so the bias cannot be signed. Safe form: 'Under classical nondifferential contamination it would attenuate, but onset is unobserved, so I cannot sign the bias. The coefficient is an announcement-anchored average association, not an identified effect of negotiation exposure.'
findings_that_change_what_to_say_not_wha.F02: 'No pre-trend' was inferred from one insignificant PRE2 coefficient whose approximate interval runs from about -0.028 to 0.042. Safe form: 'no statistically detected elevation at PRE2', which is consistent with a concentrated PRE1 pattern without proving the absence of earlier drift.
findings_that_change_what_to_say_not_wha.where_these_go: The speaker notes. Both must be written in the safe form and never in the flat form.
